title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: The riveting first-person narrative of Kvothe, a legendary wizard and musician who recounts his extraordinary life from his humble beginnings to his rise as the most notorious wizard of his age.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Set in the distant future, a noble family takes control of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the universe's most precious resource. A sweeping tale of politics, religion, and survival.

author: George Orwell
description: A chilling dystopian novel set in a totalitarian society ruled by Big Brother, where independent thinking is a crime and reality itself is manipulated by the state.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young Andalusian shepherd embarks on a journey to find a worldly treasure, only to discover that the real treasure lies within himself. A timeless fable about following your dreams.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Through the eyes of young Scout Finch, this Pulitzer Prize-winning novel explores themes of racial injustice and moral growth in the American Deep South during the 1930s.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A groundbreaking narrative of humanity's creation and evolution, from the Stone Age to the modern era. Harari explores how biology and history have defined us and enhanced our understanding of what it means to be human.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: Stephen Hawking's landmark work explains complex topics in cosmology — the Big Bang, black holes, the nature of time — in a way that is accessible to general readers.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: An exploration of the gene from Gregor Mendel's pea plants to CRISPR, weaving together science, history, and ethics in this compelling account of one of the most powerful ideas in biology.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: Richard Dawkins' classic work introduces the gene-centered view of evolution, coining the concept of the meme and transforming how we think about natural selection and human behavior.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: Carl Sagan's iconic exploration of the universe covers the origin of life, the nature of consciousness, and humanity's place in the vast cosmic arena, written with breathtaking elegance.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
description: The story of Henrietta Lacks, whose cancer cells were taken without her knowledge in 1951 and became one of the most important tools in medicine, raising profound questions about race, ethics, and science.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship that teaches developers how to write readable, maintainable, and efficient code. Essential reading for every serious programmer.
